title: How Rich Thy Gifts, Almighty King
description: How Rich Thy Gifts, Almighty King in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Andrew Kippis wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 885 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Thanksgiving for National Prosperity”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: How rich thy gifts, Al-might-y King! From thee our pub-lic bless-ings spring; Th'ex-tend-ed trade, the fruit-ful skies, The trea-sures lib-er-ty be-stows, Th'e-ter-nal joys the gos-pel shows, All from thy bound-less good-ness rise.

lines: How rich thy gifts, Almighty King!
From thee our public blessings spring;
Th' extended trade, the fruitful skies,
The treasures liberty bestows,
Th' eternal joys the gospel shows, —
All from thy boundless goodness rise.
Here commerce spreads the wealthy store,
Which pours from every foreign shore;
Science and art their charms display;
Religion teaches us to raise
Our voices to our Maker's praise,
As truth and conscience point the way.
With grateful hearts, with joyful tongues,
To God we raise united songs;
His power and mercy we proclaim;
This land through every age shall own,
Jehovah here has fixed his throne,
And triumph in his mighty name.
Long as the moon her course shall run,
Or man behold the circling sun,
O, still may God amidst us reign;
Crown our just counsels with success,
With peace and joy our borders bless,
And all our sacred rights maintain.

licence: Public domain: Andrew Kippis died in 1795.
credits: Words by Andrew Kippis (1725–1795), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
